key_insight: A configurable chemical validity operator turns heuristic oxidation-state rules into a tunable prior that screens and guides generative materials models toward more physically plausible compositions.
engineering_relevance: This improves reliability of ultra-high-throughput materials discovery by filtering unrealistic outputs while preserving promising low-energy candidates and enabling reward-based guidance during generation.
method: Built on SMACT to encode oxidation-state chemistry as a data-informed validity filter with adjustable strictness.
Benchmarked six generative crystal models to assess stoichiometry, oxidation-state realism, and post-filtering retention near the convex hull.
Applied the same operator as a reinforcement-learning reward to steer a latent diffusion model toward chemically grounded outputs.
evidence_signal: Benchmarking showed most models captured stoichiometry but under-represented realistic oxidation-state combinations, and filtering removed rare oxidation-state compositions while keeping low-energy compounds near the convex hull.
watch_item: Chemical validity thresholds are configurable and data-informed, so overly conservative settings may exclude novel but plausible compositions or bias exploration.
paper_title: Chemical filters for ultra-high-throughput materials screening and generation
